data.narrative:
Astrolight, a Seed-stage Space & Aerospace company founded by Laurynas Mačiulis, has raised €2.8M to date. The sector includes 5 public comparables (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 observable private peers ranging from SpaceX to Planet Labs, though narrow peer filtering yields insufficient matches at identical stage and valuation tier for direct median benchmarking.

Given data constraints, Stage-Progression methodology provides the primary quantitative anchor. Using total capital raised (€2.8M ≈ $3M) as a proxy for post-seed valuation baseline, a typical 2.5x step-up multiplier to the next funding stage implies a $7M valuation. Public-comp anchoring via Space & Aerospace P/S median (27.4x across the 6-ticker set) cannot be applied without disclosed revenue figures, which private companies rarely provide at Seed stage. Peer-median triangulation is similarly inapplicable due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables meeting minimum dataset requirements (0 qualified matches; 3+ required).

The analysis supports a valuation range of $6M–$8M, centered at $7M, with material uncertainty reflecting reliance on a single methodological leg. Key sensitivities include: (1) the appropriateness of 2.5x stage progression in the current capital environment; (2) absence of revenue or unit economics to anchor public-market multiples; and (3) whether Astrolight's specific technical or commercial profile justifies departure from stage-median assumptions. Additional data on burn rate and pathway to Series A would materially improve precision.
